handlers.description: Asynchronous handlers: triggers, jobs, and schedules.

sourceMap.description:

workflows.description: Durable workflows, by name. Their steps are handlers with `workflow` triggers.

AuthConfig.description:
The roles and API key scopes an app declares. Routes may only require declared ones, so a typo
is a validation error instead of a route nobody can call.

profile.description:
User profile fields the app reads (`email`, `name`, custom claims), resolved by the
platform for the caller and readable for any user of the tenant.

ChannelDecl.description: A realtime channel: clients subscribe by key, plans publish messages to it.

key.description: Fields that identify one stream of the channel, for example `{ roomId }`.

ComputedPart.description: A computed index part: a pure expression over the row, bound to `var`.

name.description: A name for the part, for diagnostics and docs.

var.description: The variable the row is bound to.

credentials.description: Whether browsers may send cookies and auth headers.

headers.description: Extra request headers allowed (`content-type`, `authorization`, and `idempotency-key` always are).

maxAgeS.description: How long browsers may cache a preflight answer, in seconds.

origins.description: Allowed origins, like `https://app.example.com`, or `*` for any.

Counter.description: A counter over the rows of an entity, grouped by some of its fields.

agg.description:
Track the smallest or largest value of a field, or how many distinct values it has,
instead of counting rows.

groupBy.description:
What the count is grouped by: fields, or values computed from the row (like the day of a
timestamp, for time-bucketed counts).

shards.description:
Spread a hot count over this many shards (2-64), so concurrent writers rarely conflict.
Reads sum the shards.

sum.description: Sum this integer expression over the rows instead of counting them.

where.description: Only rows matching this predicate are counted.

CounterAgg.description: A derived aggregate a counter maintains instead of a count.

field.description: The field (a string, int, decimal, bool, enum, id, or timestamp).

CronScan.description: The rows a scanning cron walks through.

index.description: Scan this index instead of the primary key.

prefix.description: Constant values for a prefix of the scanned fields.

CronSchedule.description: A calendar schedule: a five-field cron expression in a time zone.

cron.description: `minute hour day-of-month month weekday`, like `0 9 * * mon`.

Dedupe.description: Where a webhook delivery's event id is.

bodyField.description: A top-level body field holding the event id.

header.description: A header holding the event id, lowercase.

ttlMs.description: How long event ids are remembered, in milliseconds (at most 7 days).

DefaultValue.description: How a missing field gets its value.

oneOf.description: A constant value.
The current time (timestamp fields only).
A newly generated id (id fields only).

Entity.description: A stored entity: a schema plus an ordered primary key.

deprecated.description: Marks the entity deprecated, with a note. A later revision may then remove it.

invariants.description:
Rules every row must satisfy, by name. Checked on every write; a write that breaks one
fails the request and rolls back.

key.description:
Primary key fields, in order. Rows are stored sorted by this key, so a prefix of the key
selects a contiguous range.

mutable.description: `false` for append-only entities: rows can be inserted but never updated or deleted.

ttl.description: Rows expire: they're invisible once `field + ms` has passed, and swept in the background.

versioned.description:
Keeps an int `version` field: 1 on insert, incremented on every update. Updates can
require an expected version (optimistic concurrency for clients).

details.description:
Data the error carries, returned as `details`. Every `fail` and `ensure` of this error
provides the required fields.

message.description: Human-readable message returned to the client.

EventDecl.description: A declared event with a typed payload.

ExampleExpect.description:
What an example expects. Bodies and deliveries match as subsets: listed keys must be equal,
others are ignored; arrays match item by item.

body.description: A subset of the response body.

deliveries.description: With `process`: the deliveries made, in any order (each a subset).

runs.description: With `process`: the handlers that ran, in any order.

ExampleRequest.description: An example's request: the route's method and path are implied.

default.description: Value used when the field isn't provided.

deprecated.description: Marks the field deprecated, with a note. A later revision may then remove it.

optional.description: Whether the field may be absent (stored as `null`).

Handler.description: A handler: a plan run asynchronously when something happens.

errors.description: Declared errors. Failing with one counts as a failed attempt, which is retried.

plan.description: The handler's logic. Its output is ignored.

Idempotency.description:
Idempotency settings for a route. A successful response is stored with the request's key in
the same transaction as the route's writes, and replayed for the same key within `ttl_ms`.

required.description: Whether requests without an idempotency key are rejected.

ttlMs.description: How long a stored response is replayed, in milliseconds (at most 7 days).

fields.description:

optionally with a range on the next one.

unique.description: At most one row per indexed value. Rows with a `null` part aren't constrained.

where.description: Only rows matching this predicate are indexed (a partial index).

IndexPart.description: One part of an index: a field, or a value computed from the row.

anyOf.description: A computed value, such as a lowercased email.

Input.description: Route inputs. Every input is validated before the plan runs.

params.description: Path parameters. Must match the `:name` segments of the path exactly.

InputSource.description: Where an input value comes from.

oneOf.description: A handler's payload.

Integration.description: A declared integration: the only way plans reach the outside world.

config.description: Provider configuration (base URL, secret names, ...), interpreted by the platform.

provider.description: Which provider implements it, for example `"http"`, `"email"`, `"stripe"`.

output.description: Output fields (calls only). The response is validated against them.

Literal.description: A constant value in a manifest.

Plan.description:
A route's logic: statements followed by the value returned to the caller.

A plan runs as **one optimistic transaction**. A statement that fails rolls it back.

QueryRange.description:
Bounds on the field after a query's prefix. At most one lower and one upper bound. Like SQL
comparisons, a range never matches rows where that field is `null`.

maxBackoffMs.description: The longest delay between retries, in milliseconds.

retries.description: How many times a failed job is retried (at most 10).

deprecated.description: Marks the route deprecated, with a note for clients. Responses carry `Deprecation: true`.

description.description: What the route does, for generated API docs and MCP tools.

errors.description: Declared business errors the plan may fail with, by name.

examples.description:
Worked examples: given some data, this request gets this response. Documentation and
tests (`aleph test`); never part of what runs.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the manifest.

idempotency.description: Replays successful responses for repeated idempotency keys.

mcp.description: Exposes the route as an MCP tool with the same inputs, auth, and limits.

rateLimit.description: Limits how often the route may be called.

returns.description:
The declared response type. The checker verifies the plan's responses match it, and
generated clients use it.

version.description: An API version label for docs, such as `"2024-06-01"`.

webhook.description:
Makes the route an inbound webhook: the signature is verified before the plan runs, and
repeated deliveries of one event run once.

RouteExample.description: A worked example of a route.

given.description: Rows that exist before the request, by entity.

mocks.description: Integration responses (`{ integration, operation, response | error }`).

process.description: Run the async work the request caused (handlers, deliveries) before checking.

secrets.description:
Test secret values (webhook signing keys), by name. Never real secrets: examples ship in
the manifest.

users.description: User profiles in the directory, by user id.

onTimeout.description: The step to run on timeout.

then.description: The step to run when the signal arrives.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait, in milliseconds (at most 30 days).

TimePart.description: Parts of a point in time, in a time zone.

oneOf.description: Day of the month, 1-31.

Trigger.description:
What runs a handler. The handler reads its payload with `input` expressions of source
`payload`:
- `event`, `queue`: the declared payload fields
- `deadLetter`: the job's payload fields, plus `error` and `attempts`
- `entity`: `before` and `after` (rows, `null` when absent)
- `cron`: `firedAt`, plus `batch` (a list of rows) when it scans
- `workflow`: `instanceId`, `input`, `state`, `signals` (the signal that resumed the step, by
  name; the others are `null`), and `error` (in a compensation step)

oneOf.description: An emitted event.
A committed change to a row.
A job on a queue. At most one handler per queue.
A job that failed every retry.

One step of a workflow. It ends by moving to another step (`next`), waiting for a
signal (`waitFor`), or finishing (`complete`); a step that ends without one completes.

onFail.description:
The step to run if this one fails every retry (a compensating action). Without one,
the workflow fails.

oneOf.description: A schedule: runs at every multiple of `every_ms` (plus `offset_ms`) since the epoch.

everyMs.description: Interval, in milliseconds (1 second to 30 days). Ignored (and 0) with `schedule`.

offsetMs.description: Offset into each interval, in milliseconds.

scan.description:
Run once per batch of an entity's rows instead of once per tick. The platform
paginates: each batch is a separate, separately-bounded execution.

schedule.description: A calendar schedule instead of an interval.

field.description: A timestamp field the lifetime counts from, such as `createdAt`.

ms.description: How long rows live after it, in milliseconds.

Verify.description:
A webhook signature scheme. `secret` names a secret the platform holds; the manifest never
contains secret values.

oneOf.description: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body (or of `timestamp.body`) in a header.

prefix.description: Text before the signature in the header, such as `sha256=`.

timestampHeader.description:
A header with the delivery time in seconds. When set, the signed text is
`timestamp.body` and stale deliveries are rejected.

toleranceS.description: How old a delivery may be, in seconds (default 300).

oneOf.description: Stripe's `Stripe-Signature` scheme.

toleranceS.description: How old a delivery may be, in seconds (default 300).

oneOf.description: GitHub's `X-Hub-Signature-256` scheme.

Webhook.description: An inbound webhook: how to verify deliveries, and how to recognize repeats.

dedupe.description: Runs each event once: later deliveries with the same event id get the first response.

WorkflowDecl.description:
A durable workflow: steps that run one after another, each its own bounded transaction, with
typed state carried between them, waits for signals with timeouts, delays, retries, and
compensation. Instances are identified by a key the starter chooses.

backoffMs.description: Delay before a step's first retry, in milliseconds.

input.description: What a workflow is started with (read-only afterwards).

maxSteps.description: The most steps one instance may run (1-1000), so every instance finishes.

retries.description: Retries of a failed step (at most 10), with exponential backoff.

signals.description: Signals the workflow can wait for, with their payloads.

state.description: State carried between steps. Every field is optional: it starts `null`, and steps set it.
